comment: Hidden groups (M3-01), run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js and tests/test_state.py.
A rule implemented in two languages gets one fixture (engineering rule, dev branch).
`parse` cases: the raw JSON value of state.json's `hiddenGroups` and the list
both readers must produce. `cap` pins MAX_HIDDEN_GROUPS by generating a list
one longer than it in the test, so the number lives in the sources and here.
`browse` cases are JavaScript only: python has no scope logic. Each is a
channel list, a hidden list, and what All / a group / search must return,
asserted through channelsForScope and filterChannels -- the real path.
`groups` is the GROUPS section, which exists only when two or more groups are VISIBLE (GS3): a lone survivor lists no section.
`hide` cases (D-STATE-2) join the two runtimes through what each WRITES:
the raw group-title, the group the helper's parse writes for it, the name
hiding that group stores, and `storedBefore`, the name 0.17.0's shell
stored hiding it (the engine's trim of the helper's group, as Qt's V4
reads it). Python parses the title, and reads the group, the stored name
and storedBefore back through normalize_hidden_groups, as every CLI state
write does; JavaScript takes the stored name from primaryGroup and
toggleHiddenGroup, reads the group and storedBefore through
hiddenGroupList, and hides the row with each. Both readers take
url-whitespace.json's union off a name's edges, which holds every member
of either engine's own whitespace, so a name any earlier writer stored
reads as the group it hid. Until D-STATE-2 the shell trimmed with the
engine's whitespace, so a group-title `<FEFF><U+001C>Sports` was stored as
`<U+001C>Sports`, the next CLI write stored `Sports`, and the group was
shown again.
The union's cost, stated: groups 0.17.0 listed apart can list as one.
`<FEFF><U+001C>Sports`, `Sports<U+001C><FEFF>` and `Sports` are all
`Sports` now, so a name 0.17.0 stored for any of them hides all three; and
a group that strips to nothing, such as `<FEFF><U+001C><FEFF>`, lists as
Ungrouped, so the `<U+001C>` 0.17.0 stored hiding it is dropped (the
helper's next CLI write already dropped it).

parse.name: a string is not a list
an object is not a list
case is not folded (a group name is exact)
Ungrouped is a name like any other
D-STATE-2: the reader's whitespace comes off both ends, U+001C, U+0085 and U+FEFF among it, in any order

browse.name: nothing hidden: All is the list itself
one hidden group leaves All, keeps its own scope
a hidden name absent from this source shows no entry and hides nothing
the primary group decides: a second group after ; does not hide
hiding Ungrouped hides the channels with no group
D-STATE-2: a group the helper wrote behind a U+FEFF is hidden by the name 0.17.0 stored for it, which reads as the name hiding it stores now

hide.name: D-STATE-2, the measured case: a group-title starting U+FEFF U+001C is written as it stands, and hiding it stores the name without either
Python's whitespace at a group-title's edge is the helper's to strip, so the shell finds nothing left to strip
the first of two groups is written with its U+FEFF, and both sides read it without
ideographic space and medium mathematical space come off both ends
split_groups strips each group, so a U+0085 before the `;` is the helper's to take
